title: Impact of Wilderness Designation on Deforestation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is appropriate here since wilderness designation is determined by an elevation cutoff. The key assumption is that areas just below and above the elevation threshold are comparable in all unobservable characteristics except for wilderness designation. We expect a discontinuous jump in deforestation rates at the cutoff, with lower rates in designated wilderness areas.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s93_data.csv")

# First, identify the cutoff by examining the treatment assignment
cutoff <- min(data$running_var[data$treated == 1])
print(paste("Estimated cutoff:", cutoff))

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print("Main RDD Results:")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
print(paste("Treatment Effect (RDD Coefficient):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))

# Visual inspection - RDD plot
rdd_plot <- rdplot(y = data$y, x = data$running_var_centered, c = 0,
                   title = "RDD: Wilderness Designation and Deforestation",
                   x.label = "Elevation (centered)", 
                   y.label = "Deforestation Rate")

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Different bandwidth selection
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var_centered, c = 0, 
                        h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 0.5)
print("Half bandwidth:")
print(paste("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4)))

rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var_centered, c = 0, 
                          h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 2)
print("Double bandwidth:")
print(paste("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_double_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_quadratic <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var_centered, c = 0, p = 2)
print("Quadratic polynomial:")
print(paste("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_quadratic$coef[1], 4)))

# 3. McCrary density test for manipulation
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print("McCrary Density Test p-value:")
print(paste("P-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4)))

# Summary statistics around cutoff
print("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
treated_mean <- mean(data$y[data$treated == 1])
control_mean <- mean(data$y[data$treated == 0])
print(paste("Mean deforestation - Treated (wilderness):", round(treated_mean, 4)))
print(paste("Mean deforestation - Control (non-wilderness):", round(control_mean, 4)))
print(paste("Simple difference:", round(treated_mean - control_mean, 4)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative treatment effect (coefficient around -0.1 to -0.3), indicating that wilderness designation reduces deforestation rates. This makes economic sense as wilderness areas have legal protections against logging and development. The magnitude should be meaningful but not extreme, as some deforestation might still occur through natural processes or enforcement gaps. The RDD approach should show a clear discontinuous drop in deforestation rates at the elevation cutoff where wilderness designation begins.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare deforestation rates just above and below the elevation cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Wilderness designation is associated with a moderate increase in deforestation rates.
